text:
kevin: Posting results from today's QAT vs post-quant sweep for LumenEmbed-v2. TL;DR: QAT-int6 narrows the recall@10 gap vs float32 a lot (0.852 -> 0.839) compared to naive int6-PQ (0.802). But short queries still suffer. Plots: https://internal.s3/lumen/qatsweep/3891234567/summary.png :bar_chart:
anika: Nice. Did you train with contrastive loss only or mixed with margin/rerank loss?
kevin: Mixed loss: contrastive + small cross-encoder distill term for top-10. Training config below. Also did a paired eval on reranker-rescoring (tiny cross-encoder) to see hybrid impact.
```bash
# training cmd (simplified)
python train.py \\\
  --model lumen-encoder-v2 \\\
  --loss contrastive+distill \\\
  --qat true --qat-bits 6 \\\
  --opq false --pq-m 16 \\\
  --batch 1024 --lr 2e-5 \\\
  --holdout holdout-50k.jsonl
```
kevin: Eval commands: mean pooling, cls, and weighted-mean (attn pool) all tried. Best QAT config used weighted-mean pooling + L2 norm. Eval: recall@1,5,10 / mrr / silhouette / idflip-rate.
peggy: How much does the reranker help tail cohorts (short queries / faq)?
kevin: Rerank (cross-encoder tiny) rescoring top-100 closes almost all short-query gap: int6-QAT+rerank recall@10 short=0.823 vs float32+rerank 0.831. The cost is extra CPU per request; we simulated async rerank where feasible.
sam: Can you share idflip-rate metric? We saw weird neighbor swaps earlier when PQ interacts with whitening.
kevin: idflip-rate (k=10) float32=0.012, QAT-int6=0.018, naive-PQ-int6=0.045. So QAT helps a lot over naive post-quant. Silhouette (kmeans k=300) float32=0.44, QAT=0.40, naive-PQ=0.29.
anika: Good. Any experiments with small-ensemble (avg of last2 layers) to stabilise short queries without big index cost?
kevin: Yes: last2-avg (512->norm) + QAT-int6 = recall@10 0.846 and short 0.80. Index size +8% vs baseline. Combining last2-avg + rerank yields almost parity for short queries.
peggy: What about OPQ/PQ after QAT? Is it redundant?
kevin: We tried QAT -> OPQ(32) -> PQ(m=8) as a compact pipeline: recall@10 0.835 (slightly less than QAT alone), but index size reduced ~2x vs last2 ensemble. So tradeoffs remain.
sam: Did you check multilingual cohorts and temporal drift (recent docs)?
kevin: Multilang (es/fr) stable ~-0.01 delta. Temporal drift on docs added in last 30 days shows small recall drop for PQ-flow; idflip concentrated in newly added anchors. Uploaded cohort CSV: https://internal.s3/lumen/qatsweep/3891234567/cohort_breakdown.csv
ops-bot: Regression scanner: flagged cohorts short_queries delta -0.035 (recall@10) and faq-anchors delta -0.028. Annotated status=needs-triage.
anika: Proposed rollout: default onboard with QAT-int8 for most endpoints. Offer QAT-int6 as experimental compact config but require rerank or last2-avg precompute for short-query sensitive routes. Gate: silhouette >= 0.38 and idflip <= 0.03 for int6 candidates.
peggy: Agree. Also add a synthetic augmentation step (paraphrase short queries) during QAT to bias codebooks to short queries. Might reduce the need for rerank.
kevin: I'll run two overnight jobs: 1) QAT with short-query augmentation (job id qaj-3891234567-1), 2) QAT-int6 + OPQ pipeline grid for smaller indices (job id qaj-3891234567-2). Will push recommended config + cohort CSV in a PR tomorrow.
sam: For canary: suggest hybrid routing where traffic with query_length<=6 goes to rerank path. Start at 0.5% traffic. Measure live recall via sampled labeled pairs.
anika: Also add a unit eval: idflip_rate(k=10) <= 0.03 and silhouette >= 0.38 for any int6 pass. Block int6 auto-rollout if failed.
ops-bot: Scheduled fuzzcheck jobs qaj-3891234567-1 and qaj-3891234567-2. ETA results ~9-11h.
